requirements.quote: After running a Quarter Round on these four numbers, we get these:
Note that only the numbers in positions 2, 7, 8, and 13 changed.

exclusions.quote: Words 13-15 are a nonce, which MUST not be repeated for the same key.
exclusions.reason: this fixture checks the quarter round only

exclusions.quote: The pair (r,s) should be unique, and MUST be unpredictable for each invocation (that is why it was originally obtained by encrypting a nonce), while "r" MAY be constant, but needs to be modified as follows before being used: ("r" is treated as a 16-octet little-endian number):
exclusions.reason: this fixture checks the quarter round only

exclusions.quote: Any document that specifies the use of Poly1305 as a MAC algorithm for some protocol MUST specify that 256 bits are allocated for the integrity key.
exclusions.reason: this fixture checks the quarter round only

exclusions.quote: This MUST be unique per invocation with the same key, so it MUST NOT be randomly generated.
exclusions.reason: this fixture checks the quarter round only

exclusions.quote: Additionally, any protocol using this algorithm MUST include the complete tag to minimize the opportunity for forgery.
exclusions.reason: this fixture checks the quarter round only

exclusions.quote: Tag truncation MUST NOT be done.
exclusions.reason: this fixture checks the quarter round only

exclusions.quote: The Poly1305 key MUST be unpredictable to an attacker.
exclusions.reason: this fixture checks the quarter round only

exclusions.quote: For this reason, with online protocols, implementation MUST use a constant-time comparison function rather than relying on optimized but insecure library functions such as the C language's memcmp().
exclusions.reason: this fixture checks the quarter round only
